name: Centrifugal Lipodystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive, localized loss of subcutaneous fat starting at the scalp vertex and spreading centrifugally
Skin biopsy showing lipoatrophy with minimal inflammation and absence of scarring
Exclusion of other generalized or partial lipodystrophies and connective tissue diseases
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating localized subcutaneous fat loss without underlying bone involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation with histopathological confirmation and exclusion of other lipodystrophies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing localized subcutaneous fat loss without underlying bone or muscle involvement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; genetic testing typically non-diagnostic
other: Histopathology showing lipoatrophy with minimal inflammation and no fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of skin induration and sclerosis
Hemifacial atrophy involving skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, and bone
Neurological symptoms such as seizures or headaches
Widespread fat loss affecting trunk and limbs
Metabolic complications such as insulin resistance

redFlags: Rapid progression of fat loss beyond scalp
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Signs of underlying connective tissue disease or systemic sclerosis
references: Kumar S, et al. Centrifugal lipodystrophy: clinical and histopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
